subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

She was adding to the confusion by making contradictory statements.
solution:
No substitution is required.

Add to means to increase something. \'Adding to the confusion\' correctly means making the confusion greater.

\'Add with\', \'add in\' and \'add on\' do not give this meaning here.

Correct sentence: She was adding to the confusion by making contradictory statements.
conceptTested: The phrasal verb 'add to' means to increase or intensify something (e.g., adding to the confusion).

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

The teacher directed the students to submit their assignments before the deadline.

options.C: directed to the students to submit
options.c: directed to the students to submit

solution:
No substitution is required.

In the sense of instructing, direct + person + to - infinitive is the correct pattern: directed the students to submit.

The other options use a wrong preposition or put \'to\' before the object.

Correct sentence: The teacher directed the students to submit their assignments before the deadline.
conceptTested: The verb 'direct' takes a direct object followed by a to-infinitive (direct + person + to-infinitive).

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.

The executive council has reached to a unanimous decision regarding the acquisition of the rival firm after months of negotiation.
solution:
Use has reached.

\'Reach\' takes a direct object without \'to\': reach a decision. \'The executive council\' is a singular collective noun here, so \'has\' is correct.
Correct sentence: The executive council has reached a unanimous decision regarding the acquisition of the rival firm after months of negotiation.
conceptTested: The verb 'reach' is transitive and takes a direct object without a preposition like 'to'. Collective nouns acting as a single unit take singular verbs.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.

She is considered the most intelligent of the two architects who designed the sustainable skyscraper project for the new business district.

options.B: the more intelligent of the two
options.b: the more intelligent of the two

solution:
Use the more intelligent of the two.

When exactly two people are compared, use the comparative (more) with \'the ... of the two\'; the superlative (most) is for three or more.

Correct sentence: She is considered the more intelligent of the two architects who designed the sustainable skyscraper project for the new business district.
conceptTested: Comparative degree (more ... of the two) is used when comparing exactly two entities, whereas superlative degree is used for three or more.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.

I prefer to analyze the raw data personally to relying on the subjective interpretations provided by the junior researchers.
solution:
Prefer compares two actions with the pattern prefer + -ing ... to + -ing; “prefer ... than” is not standard.

The sentence already has “to relying”, so the first action should also be a gerund: “analyzing”.

Correct sentence: I prefer analyzing the raw data personally to relying on the subjective interpretations provided by the junior researchers.
Therefore, the best improvement is I prefer analyzing.
conceptTested: The verb 'prefer' follows the structure prefer + gerund (... to + gerund) when comparing two activities.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The committee concluded that the proposal was not acceptable nor was it feasible for implementation.

options.A: not acceptable nor was it feasible
options.a: not acceptable nor was it feasible

solution:
Rule: “Nor” pairs with “neither”, not with “not”. The correlative pair must join parallel words: neither acceptable nor feasible.
Correct sentence: The committee concluded that the proposal was neither acceptable nor feasible for implementation.
conceptTested: The correlative conjunction pair 'neither' must be followed by 'nor', maintaining parallel grammatical structures.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

The cab turned to an alley to avoid the traffic jam.
solution:
Rule: “Into” shows movement from outside to inside. The cab moved into the alley, so “turned into an alley” is correct.
Correct sentence: The cab turned into an alley to avoid the traffic jam.
conceptTested: Verbs of motion like 'turned' take the preposition 'into' to indicate movement from the outside to the inside of a confined space.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

I know it takes a lot of courage to stand up to bullies, but you must try.
solution:
Stand up to means to resist or confront someone powerful. This is exactly what is needed against bullies, so no substitution is required.

Option meanings: Stand up for - to support or defend someone or something

Stand up with - not an idiomatic phrase in this sense

Stand up as - not an idiomatic phrase in this sense
conceptTested: The phrasal verb 'stand up to' means to confront or resist powerfully, making it the appropriate idiom for dealing with bullies.

subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.

He is superior than his contemporaries in the field of theoretical physics and quantum mechanics due to his innovative research.
solution:
Rule: Latin comparatives such as superior, inferior, senior, junior and prior take “to”, not “than”, and are never used with “more” or “most”.
Correct sentence: He is superior to his contemporaries in the field of theoretical physics and quantum mechanics due to his innovative research.
conceptTested: Latin comparative adjectives (superior, inferior, senior, junior) are followed by 'to' instead of 'than' and do not take 'more' or 'most'.
